# Jeremiah 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** These are the words of Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah — one of the priests from the town of Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin.

**2** The LORD's message first came to him during the reign of King Josiah son of Amon of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his rule.

**3** It continued through the reign of King Jehoiakim son of Josiah, and all the way to the end of the eleventh year of King Zedekiah son of Josiah — right up until Jerusalem was taken into exile in the fifth month.

**4** The LORD spoke to me and said:

**5** "I knew you before I formed you in your mother's womb. Before you were born, I set you apart. I appointed you to be My spokesman to the nations."

**6** I protested, "Lord GOD, I don't know how to speak! I'm too young for this!"

**7** But the LORD told me, "Don't say that you're too young. You will go wherever I send you, and you will say whatever I tell you to say.

**8** Don't be afraid of anyone. I am with you, and I will protect you." This is the LORD's declaration.

**9** Then the LORD reached out and touched my mouth and said, "There — I have placed My words in your mouth.

**10** Today I am giving you authority over nations and kingdoms. You will uproot and tear down, destroy and overthrow — but also build and plant."

**11** Then the LORD asked me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I answered, "I see the branch of an almond tree."

**12** The LORD said, "You've seen correctly, because I am watching over My word to make sure it happens."

**13** The LORD spoke to me again: "What do you see?" I said, "I see a pot boiling over, tilting from the north."

**14** The LORD said, "From the north, disaster will pour out on everyone living in this land.

**15** I am about to summon all the armies of the northern kingdoms," declares the LORD. "Their kings will come and set up their thrones at the gates of Jerusalem, against her walls, and against every town in Judah.

**16** I will pronounce My verdict on My people for all the evil they've done — abandoning Me, burning incense to foreign gods, and worshiping things they made with their own hands.

**17** So get ready! Stand up and tell them everything I command you. Don't let them intimidate you, or I will give them real reason to intimidate you.

**18** As of today, I am making you like a fortified city, an iron pillar, and a bronze wall — standing against the entire land: against Judah's kings, officials, priests, and all the people.

**19** They will fight you, but they will never defeat you, because I am with you and I will rescue you." This is the LORD's declaration.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **1:5-6**: Jeremiah's call is intensely personal — God knew him before birth. His 'I'm too young' objection is raw and relatable, and God doesn't argue with the feeling — He just overrides it.

- **1:10**: The six verbs of Jeremiah's mission are telling — four are about tearing things down, only two about building. This prophet's main job is demolition before reconstruction.

- **1:18-19**: God turns Jeremiah into a walking fortress. The whole nation will come at him, but he'll stand. It's a promise, but it's also a warning — this ministry will be a battle.

— PNEUMA
